problemStatement.formal: \text{For a }2\times2\text{ system }Ax=b\text{ over a division ring }D\text{, define }|A|_{00}=a_{00}-a_{01}a_{11}^{-1}a_{10}.\text{ Prove }x_0=|A|_{00}^{-1}(b_0-a_{01}a_{11}^{-1}b_1)\text{ gives the quasideterminant solution, prove uniqueness, and show the commutative specialization recovers classical Cramer's Rule.}
problemStatement.plain: Formalize the 2x2 non-commutative analogue of Cramer's Rule over a division ring using Gelfand-Retakh quasideterminants, including the explicit solution, uniqueness, and the field case that reduces to the classical theorem.
whyMatters: Quasideterminants are the determinant-like tool available for non-commutative linear algebra.
The 2x2 case is a tractable first formalization of a Gelfand-Retakh construction.
A completed proof would test DivisionRing matrix algebra and clarify how the commutative specialization relates back to classical Cramer's Rule.

proven: The gallery already contains the classical commutative Cramer's Rule and related adjugate/cofactor and overdetermined-system entries.
The local problem notes give the explicit 2x2 quasideterminant formula as a Schur-complement expression.
open: The 2x2 non-commutative solution formula, uniqueness proof, and commutative specialization are not yet recorded as completed Lean work in the local evidence.
